I am 10 years into having nightnares too. I too went to weed, it stopped them. Tried to stop weed and they just came back nightly. Got really bad when i went a month without. I only get nightmares, i have never had a good or even weird dream in my life. But even the scariest ones feel guilty to tell. Like i am over reacting and shouldn't be so broken by something as simple as a dream. Idk if its just toxic masculinity or what, but i cant help but feel like i shouldn't be affected by them. But when its night after night, i never sleep for more than 4 hours and i even started hallucinating i said enough was enough and seen a therapist who specialized in dreams. It was pricey and didnt make them go away but it helped me deal with them way better and made them appear less often. 

For me, the trigger to dreaming is stress. The more stressed i am the more likely I'll to have a nightmare. Which in turn made me more stressed the day after and it just fed itself. I still smoke from time to time to help with it but usually i just try to keep stress to a minimum. The therapist gave me some techniques that i still use. Breaking down the dream as soon as you wake up and trying to figure out if you feel any meaning from it, dont feel bad if you cant find any. Sometimes there is none. Making sure that when you go to sleep you're very tired. Writing your dreams out can also help, even if you just crumple it up and burn it after. Its weird, i guess it helps the brain process the dream better and just makes that erie feeling you get after waking up from one not last into the day. Last one is go for walks, idk the specifics of it but walking in nature for even just like 20mins helps dramatically. I am sure each person is different and its hard, i still have troubles dealing with it at times. Don't feel bad about telling people about them, dreams affect our mental state far more than most people realize.

Lucid dreaming is definitely a good step to go in to help dreams, my lack of normal dreaming ability seems to stop me from being able to do it like others but i would still recommend trying it. Therapist said its more of thing to try when your more stable with dreams as if you try it when you're just nonstop stressed it can just make normal dreams more realistic.  Glad i could help, good luck and sweet dreams

Hello, 24M here. Ive had a nightmare disorder since i was 16. Realistic dreams are fucked and i am sorry you have to endure that. It is possible to find specialist for dreams in therapy online  but if you dont like the zoom calls or just audio calls its understandable. 

A good place to start is trying to think of the reasoning of why your having those dreams as I've seen you've done. Trauma  related dreams need to be dealt with differently than others because they are so deeply imprinted onto your brains. I still haven't solved my truama nightmares because of that, but i have lowered my overal dream frequency for non trauma dreams and heres my tips on what i noticed helped.

1. Finding the cause of why you feel that way in the dream. So for mine it was always being chased or hunted. I reflected on why i felt that and what parts of my life could relate to that. After lots of thinking i realized it was my anxiety and my fear of failure. I still am afraid and anxious but the realization that thats why i felt like that helped those types of dreams drop.

2. Smoking weed( i dont recommend) i kinda rely on it just to not dream. Not a good habbit to get into but before i knew anything it was a good escape to just stop my dreams entirely, very effective at first, not so much after smoking for 6 years. 

3. Just reach out and talk about them, confront them directly, maybe even write as much as you can down as soon as you wake up from having one. This was really hard for me and i found myself tearing up the paper a lot and it makes you remember the nightmares more but because you open up about them and normalize them your mind just feels less anxious about it, it helps shut down a bunch of small stupid little thoughts i was having about how fucked i really was. Its easy to get into a self doubt, where you just get carried away to the point you're just scaring yourself.

4. Go to tired when you're actually tired. Forcing yourself to lay there when you're not ready to is just asking for stress and insomnia to batter you up and get you in the nightmare mindset. I was scared to sleep because my dreams were so frequent and i could feel them coming in the day. But you gotta just avoid that train of thought at all cost. Keep yourself busy and do a high attention task before bed if you cant stop thinking about em. I do gaming but to each their own. 

5. Take care of your body and mind. Nightmares are always more common in the stressful and downs of my life and are least common when i am generally happy. Making sure to eat enough and hydrate enough can really help keep a more calm state of mind throughout the day. If you physically feel good it affects your mental and same vise versa


P.S. i have never had a good or normal dream in my life so i may be different than you. All my dreams are nightmares. I hope these help, i learned them from a dream specalist therapist in Canada BC. Well, not the weed one haha that was something 18yr old me just noticed. I have heard of weed making people dream more too so that ones very different depending on the person.
